messages:
karen: FYI mkdocs linkcheck failed on main after the SDK PR merge, 12 broken links flagged. Looks like parentheses in inline code and relative paths inside fenced blocks are being mangled.

karen: CI excerpt:
```
LinkCheckError: /sdk/python#client-setup -> 404
  Referenced from: content/sdk/python/examples.md:28
LinkCheckError: /sdk/js) -> 404
  Referenced from: content/sdk/js/quickstart.md:9
```

docs-bot: CI: linkcheck failed for commit abc123 (checks/linkcheck) :warning:

maria: This is the classic codefence+relative link issue. Quick fixes: 1) wrap example URLs in angle brackets like `<./path>` inside code blocks so the parser doesn't attempt to resolve, or 2) run a small normalization step during build to convert demo links to absolute site paths.

eli: I'll prototype a small node script to scan content/sdk and replace only links that match the demo pattern. Also plan to add a temporary linkcheck whitelist so we don't block unrelated PRs.

josh: Note: docs are versioned. If we rewrite to absolute paths we must emit redirects for older versions. I can add a tiny redirect generator to docusaurus config to map rewritten paths back to versioned URLs.

sophia: I'll audit the markdown parser plugins used in the mkdocs pipeline (markdown-it + linkify options) and check ordering. If linkify runs before fence handling that's likely the root cause. Will report back with exact plugin versions.

maria: Also recommend adding a pre-commit grep to catch patterns like "]\(\./" inside triple-backtick blocks to prevent regressions.

karen: Action items: eli/maria run normalization script and open PR `docs/link-fix-1764`; josh add redirect generator; sophia post parser findings; i'll add a short release note blurb for the docs changelog.
